purpose: Held-out evidence review; fictional. Review-only. Do not include this material in candidate inputs or publication-bound source packets.
material_findings: The packet affirmatively supports signed acceptance on 16 July, distinct from delivery on 14 July; this is not an absent-acceptance case.
The extra fee has genuine bilateral written signatures on 9 July before work began on 10 July; the buyer also accepted that work on 16 July.
Tax-inclusive contract charges total 10000; cleared receipts total 6000; invoice balance is 4000. Payment allocation leaves 2400 base and 1600 extra.
Fourteen calendar days after 16 July is 30 July, matching the record. Buyer proposed later payment but the packet contains no accepted variation of the due date.
The two minor defects were expressly compatible with acceptance and the buyer confirmed correction. Buyer expressly did not dispute the invoices.
The additional 300 collection administration charge lacks an identified contractual or invoice basis in these sources. Do not silently treat the full 4300 as equally supported.
10 August is the demand writer’s requested deadline, not a verified court or statutory deadline. No real law is supplied or needed.
verification_rationale: A sound review should preserve strong adverse evidence for the represented buyer and distinguish the well-supported invoice balance from the unsupported surcharge. Mechanical denial for missing acceptance or unapproved extras contradicts signed source evidence. Verify source references, arithmetic and due-date calculation, without inventing external law or a factual defense.
